sections.name: Title
sections.subtitle: Title Breakdown
sections.speak_en: Title breakdown. The word silhouette in Japanese comes from the French. It represents the outline of something, the shape you can see but not the details.
sections.note: Used as Naruto Shippuden OP16. The title captures the theme of chasing a dream you can barely see the outline of.

words.en_speak: silhouette. A loanword from French. The outline or shadow of something.

sections.name: Verse 1
sections.subtitle: Verse 1 — Chasing Dreams
sections.description: Running toward something you can't quite see
sections.speak_en: Verse 1. He's running toward something he can't quite see yet. The path ahead isn't clear but he keeps going.
context_lines: いつだって何だって届きそうにないから走ってきたんだろう

words.en_speak: always, no matter when. An emphatic form meaning at any time, every time.
seems like it could reach. The sou ending means it appears to or seems like.
This grammar pattern negates the seeming. It seemed reachable but actually isn't.
has been running. The te kita pattern means the action has been ongoing up until now.

grammar.explanation: Negates the appearance/likelihood. Seems like it won't happen.
grammar.example: 届きそうにない → "doesn't seem reachable"

grammar.explanation: Te-form + kita. An action that started in the past and continues to now.
grammar.example: 走ってきた → "has been running (up to now)"

trivia.title: 🎵 Naruto Shippuden OP16
trivia.text: Silhouette was used as the 16th opening theme of Naruto Shippuden, airing from 2015. It played during some of the most emotionally intense arcs of the series, cementing it as one of the most beloved anime openings of all time.

trivia.title: 📈 300 Million+ Views
trivia.text: The official music video has accumulated over 300 million views on YouTube, making it one of KANA-BOON's most popular songs globally.

podcast_script: Hey welcome back. Today we're looking at a song that... honestly, if you watched Naruto, you already know this one in your bones.
Yes! KANA-BOON. And the song is...
Shiruetto. Silhouette. And it's not just an anime opening, it's genuinely a beautiful piece of songwriting.
Let's get into the first line...
